The Battle of the Atlantic , the longest-continuous military campaign [ 11 ] [ 12 ] in World War II , ran from 1939 to the defeat of Nazi Germany in 1945, covering a major part of the naval history of World War II . At its core was the Allied naval blockade of Germany , announced the day after the declaration of war, and Germany's subsequent counterblockade. The campaign peaked from mid-1940 to the end of 1943.
